Question ID: MCR_U06_L05_GP_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.GM.2

What is the distance from (2, 5) to (9, 5)?

feedback.text: This adds the x-values. Horizontal distance is found by subtracting x-values.
Correct. The y-values match, so subtract x-values: 9 - 2 = 7.
This subtracts the y-values, but the y-values are the same.
This uses one coordinate as the distance instead of comparing both points.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U06_L05_GP_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.GM.2

What is the distance from (4, 1) to (4, 8)?

feedback.text: This uses the shared x-value as the distance. Compare y-values for vertical distance.
This adds the y-values. Distance is the difference between positions.
This subtracts 4 and 1, but vertical distance uses the y-values 1 and 8.
Correct. The x-values match, so subtract y-values: 8 - 1 = 7.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U06_L05_GP_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.GM.2

A rectangle has side lengths 6 units and 4 units. What is its perimeter?

feedback.text: Correct. Perimeter = 6 + 4 + 6 + 4 = 20 units.
This adds each different side only once. Perimeter includes all four sides.
This multiplies side lengths and uses area units.
The number is correct, but perimeter uses linear units, not square units.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U06_L05_GP_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.GM.2

A rectangle has vertices (1, 2), (6, 2), (6, 5), and (1, 5). What is its area?

feedback.text: This adds width and height. Area requires multiplication.
This is the perimeter, not the area.
Correct. Width = 6 - 1 = 5 and height = 5 - 2 = 3, so area = 15.
The number is correct, but area needs square units.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U06_L05_GP_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.GM.2

Which coordinate changes when moving vertically on the coordinate plane?

feedback.text: The x-coordinate changes when moving horizontally.
Correct. Vertical movement changes the y-coordinate.
Vertical movement keeps the x-coordinate the same.
If neither coordinate changes, the point does not move.
